summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Antigua and Barbuda documents: the 2013 Act, six amending regulations, two 2017 CIU notices, nine CIU web pages and two IMF Article IV reports. Adds fee terms and rule-change events from the legislation and the fee schedule, Iraqi naturalisation counts, and the missing IMF projection and % of GDP rows for CIP revenue.

observations.quote: To date, four individuals have been granted Antigua and Barbuda citizenship under the Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP).
observations.notes: CIU statement of 12 Apr 2016 on 'nationals of Iraq'. The four are a single applicant residing in Saudi Arabia (applied Mar 2014, approved Jul 2014) and a family of three residing in Saudi Arabia (applied Apr 2015, approved Jul 2015). The CIU statement of 4 Jul 2017 (atg-ciu-web-disparities-2017) lists Iraq with 4 applications and 6 passports to Dec 2015, which does not match two approvals and four people; that table is by 'country of origin'.

observations.quote: A family of three, residing in Saudi Arabia, who applied in April, 2015, and was approved in July, 2015.
observations.notes: One family application by Iraqi nationals resident in Saudi Arabia, filed Apr 2015, approved Jul 2015. Part of the four in the cumulative row.

program_terms.applies_to: principal applicant ($20,250 spouse; $0 child 0-11; $5,400 child 12-17; $10,800 child 18-25; $10,800 dependent parent over 65)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 9, Schedule of Fees, item 2
program_terms.quote: Due diligence fee - Principal applicant $20,250
program_terms.notes: Printed as '$'; read as EC$ (Antigua and Barbuda legislation uses EC$ unless it says otherwise; the CIU fee page prints the same amounts in ECD). Paid in full on submission with 10% of the processing fees, non-refundable (Schedule reg. 5(2)). Table replaced by S.I. 2024 No. 50 (atg-cbi-regs-2024), taken as effective 1 Aug 2024.

program_terms.applies_to: agent licence application ($13,500 on each anniversary)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 9, Schedule of Fees, item 1
program_terms.quote: a Citizenship by Investment Agent’s Licence, a fee of $8,100
program_terms.notes: Printed as '$'; read as EC$ (Antigua and Barbuda legislation uses EC$ unless it says otherwise; the CIU fee page prints the same amounts in ECD). Paid by the licensed agent, not the applicant. Annual fee $13,500; unpaid for 14 days means the licence is revoked (reg. 4(5)(b)).

program_terms.currency: days within five calendar years after registration
program_terms.applies_to: citizen by investment
program_terms.location: PDF p. 4, Act s. 4(1)
program_terms.quote: if the citizen does not spend at least 35 days in Antigua and Barbuda during the period of five calendar years after his registration
program_terms.notes: Not a price: the minimum stay. Failing it allows the Minister to deprive the person of citizenship, with no repayment of the investment (s. 4(2)). Real estate must also be held five years (Schedule reg. 6(7)).

program_terms.applies_to: family of up to four (limited time offer, NDF route)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 7, new reg. 15(2)
program_terms.quote: The processing fees in respect of an application submitted pursuant to subregulation (1) shall be $135,000 for up to a family of four members.
program_terms.notes: Printed as '$'; read as EC$ (Antigua and Barbuda legislation uses EC$ unless it says otherwise; the CIU fee page prints the same amounts in ECD). Limited time offer: NDF applications for a family of up to four filed within nine months of the Act coming into force (contribution $540,000). End date depends on the commencement order, which is not in this document. Made 11 Jul 2013, gazetted 29 Aug 2013.

events.title: Agent licences limited to citizens and long-term residents; oath can be taken abroad
events.description: S.I. 2013 No. 24 limited agent licences to citizens of Antigua and Barbuda or persons lawfully resident for at least seven years, required professional indemnity insurance of at least $3,000,000, barred members of Parliament and CIU staff (and their families), and allowed the oath of allegiance at embassies, high commissions or consulates.
events.quote: who is a citizen of Antigua and Barbuda or who is lawfully ordinarily resident for a period of not less than seven years

events.title: Dependent children up to age 29
events.description: S.I. 2017 No. 76 raised the upper age for dependent children in full-time higher education from under 26 to under 29 (definition of dependant and reg. 5(12)), alongside the temporary NDF offer of $270,000. Made 29 Nov 2017 (House resolution 9 Nov 2017), gazetted 14 Feb 2019.
events.quote: by repealing the word “twenty-six” and replacing it with the word “twenty-nine”

events.title: Dependent parents from age 58; passport renewal review fee repealed
events.description: S.I. 2019 No. 10 also lowered the age for dependent parents or grandparents from over 65 to 58 or older, repealed the Schedule of Fees item for passport renewal (five-year review), and told the Board to identify countries where marketing the programme would pay.
events.quote: who is fifty eight (58) years of age or older and who is living with and is wholly supported by the main applicant

events.title: Wider family definition, alternate main applicant and real-estate resale limit
events.description: S.I. 2024 No. 50 also redefined dependants (children up to 30, parents or grandparents over 55, unmarried siblings, spouses and children of dependants added later if the dependant is not over 35), let a main applicant designate an alternate main applicant, and allowed approved real estate to be resold to another applicant only once and only after five years. The handwritten date it was made is not legible in the scan.
events.quote: shall only be resold once for the purpose of satisfying the requirements of another applicant under the programme

gaps: S.I. 2019 No. 10 scan ends mid-amendment on PDF p. 6 (reg. 5(7)(c)); a complete copy would be needed for the rest.
The 2013 regulations end the limited time offer nine months after the Act came into force; the commencement order is not stored.
The 2017-2024 regulations refer to "Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2016" as the principal regulations; no 2016 consolidation is stored.

ledger.contains: Citizenship by Investment Act 2013 (No. 2 of 2013, gazetted 11 Apr 2013; passed House 1 Feb, Senate 19 Mar 2013) with the Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2013 in its Schedule: definitions (dependants), registration and deprivation (35-day stay in five years), six-monthly report to Parliament and its required contents, CIU and agent licensing, application procedure, ineligible applicants, investment routes (real estate $1,080,000, NDF $675,000, business $4,000,000 or $13,500,000 joint with $1,080,000 each), Schedule of Fees (agent licence $8,100/$13,500; processing and due diligence fees by family member). Route minimums, processing fee and launch event were already in the data; this pass adds the due-diligence fee, the agent licence fee and the 35-day stay rule. Criminal fines for unlicensed applications or promotion ($20,000/$15,000) and the gazette price are not programme terms and are not extracted.

Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2013 (S.I. 2013 No. 24, made 11 Jul 2013, gazetted 29 Aug 2013): new 'certified copy' definition, new agent-licensing rules (citizens or seven-year residents, $3,000,000 indemnity insurance, exclusions), document certification, oath abroad, and a limited time offer for families of up to four (NDF $540,000, processing fees $135,000). PDF p. 8 is a blank/bleed-through page. The NDF offer and price-change event were already in the data; this pass adds the offer's processing fee and a rule-change event for agents and the oath.

Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017 No. 76, made 29 Nov 2017, gazetted 14 Feb 2019): dependent-child age limit 26 to 29, and a temporary NDF offer for 1 Nov 2017 to 31 Oct 2018 ($270,000 single or family of up to four; $337,750 for five or more). The NDF term was already in the data; this pass adds the age-limit event.

Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2018 (S.I. 2018 No. 16, made 12 Jul 2018, gazetted 2 Aug 2018): adds 'investment in higher education' as a route (reg. 6A), $150,000 single or $275,000 for a family of two. Both the term and the event were already in the data; nothing else in scope.

Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019 No. 10, made and gazetted 21 Mar 2019): agents may open accounts at international banks; CIU may hold accounts outside the Eastern Caribbean and accept any currency; Board to target markets; limited time co-investment offer (two related parties, $200,000 each, real estate or dual-approved business, to 31 Oct 2019); dependent parents from age 58; passport-renewal (5-year review) fee repealed. The stored scan ends mid-sentence on PDF p. 6 (new reg. 5(7)(c) on dependants under 18), so the end of that amendment is not in the file. Co-investment term and the main event were already in the data; this pass adds the dependant-age and fee-repeal event.

Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2020 (S.I. 2020 No. 85, made and gazetted 22 Dec 2020): oath of allegiance by Zoom/Skype under set procedures, at the applicant's cost. No numbers; the event was already in the data.

Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024 No. 50, July 2024): new dependant definition, alternate main applicant, real estate US$300,000 with a single resale after five years, validation of the real-estate co-application offer (from 1 Apr 2020) and the NDF offer (since Oct 2018) to 31 Jul 2024, UWI/higher-education route US$260,000 for families of six or more, NDF US$230,000, end of all limited time offers, and a new USD fee schedule (processing, post-approval additions, due diligence, passport, five-year renewal, auxiliary services). Route amounts, processing fee and price-change event were already in the data; this pass adds due diligence, passport, renewal, dependant-addition and auxiliary fees and a rule-change event.

CIU notice to industry partners, 17 Oct 2017: the halved NDF threshold applies to applications from 1 Nov 2017; processing and due diligence fees unchanged. No numbers beyond the dates; the event was already in the data.

CIU notice to industry partners, 13 Oct 2017: government's 12 Oct 2017 announcement halving the NDF threshold (US$200,000 to US$100,000 for up to four; US$250,000 to US$125,000 for five or more); fees unchanged. The new amounts were already in the data; this pass adds the old amounts.

CIU web page on the business route (saved 28 Sep 2026): US$1,500,000 single or US$5,000,000 joint (US$400,000 each), payment timing, processing fees US$10,000 / 20,000 / +10,000 per extra dependant. The investment term was already in the data; this pass adds the processing fee.

CIU web page on the NDF route (saved 28 Sep 2026): NDF description, US$230,000 per application, who can be included, payment steps, processing fees by family size. This pass adds the contribution and processing fee as terms.

CIU web page on the real-estate route (saved 28 Sep 2026): US$300,000 minimum, processing fees, ownership through a company, five-year resale restriction, procedure. This pass adds the purchase minimum and processing fee as terms.

CIU web page on the UWI Fund route (saved 28 Sep 2026): US$260,000 for a family of six or more including processing fees, US$10,000 per dependant beyond six, one-year tuition scholarship, procedure. This pass adds the contribution as a term.

CIU Schedule of Fees page (saved 28 Sep 2026): government (processing), due diligence and passport fees explained; tables per route (NDF, real estate, business, UWI) with processing fees, contribution/investment and due diligence; due diligence and passport fees in USD and ECD; fees for adding dependants. This pass adds route minimums and fee terms (ECD amounts in notes). One cell reads '$75,000 for spouse' (likely typo, noted).

CIU statement of 12 Apr 2016: four Iraqi nationals granted citizenship to date (a single applicant approved Jul 2014 and a family of three approved Jul 2015, both resident in Saudi Arabia); Cabinet decision of 11 Dec 2014 restricting applicants from Iran, Afghanistan, Iraq, North Korea, Somalia and Yemen unless lawful permanent residents of Canada, the US or UK. The event was already in the data; this pass adds the counts (4 total; 3 in Jul 2015). The single applicant (Jul 2014) is described in words, not as a number, and is in the notes.

CIU news item of 6 Jul 2017: Canada visa requirement for Antigua and Barbuda citizens from 27 Jun 2017 and how to apply (Canadian visa fees, processing times, documents). Numbers concern Canadian visas, not the programme; the visa-access event was already in the data.

Statement of 19 Dec 2025 by the ambassador to the US on the US Proclamation of 16 Dec 2025: existing visas respected, no revocation of visas issued before 31 Dec 2025, new biometric arrangements for new applications, applying to citizens by investment too. No programme numbers; the event was already in the data.

Statement of 7 Jan 2026 on the US Visa Bond Pilot Program: applies only to a narrow category of new visitor-visa applicants; overstays by a small number of nationals; diplomatic note sent. No programme numbers; the event was already in the data.

IMF 2014 Article IV and second post-program monitoring staff report (Country Report 15/189, 89 pp.): macro, fiscal, banking (ABI Bank resolution), debt sustainability, statistical annexes. CIP content: Table 2 (cash finances 2013-15, CIP line incl. 2014 halves), Table 3 (CIP revenue EC$m 2014-2020), Table 4 (% of GDP 2014-2020), DSA annex average of about 1.9% of GDP, comparison with St. Kitts (more than 10% of GDP), recommendations (use CIP revenue for arrears and debt, transfer application fees retained by the CIU to the treasury; CIP Act bars recurrent spending). Rows already in data: 2014 63.7 / 1.9%, 2015 116 / 3.4%. Added: 2013 0.0%, 2014 H1/H2, 2016-2020 projections in EC$ and % of GDP, the DSA average and the St. Kitts comparison. Not extracted: Table 3's rounded 2014 value 64 and Table 2's 2015 116.0/3.4 (same indicator and period as existing rows); the July 2014 bond placements of about EC$39 million to MBS, PDVCAB and the NDF together (no NDF share given). Everything else (growth, debt, banking, other revenue) is out of scope.

IMF 2022 Article IV staff report (Country Report 23/184, 85 pp.): press release, staff report, annexes (external assessment, DSA, labour market, climate), statistical tables (several as images). CIP content: Table 3a (o/w CIP revenue EC$ million 2017-2027) and Table 3b (% of GDP 2017-2027), both images read by OCR; text on lower CIP revenue (EU/US scrutiny, Russia sanctions), AML/CFT and CIP agents, risk matrix, DSA stress scenario. Rows already in data: EC$ 2017-2021. Added: EC$ 2022-2027 projections and all 11 % of GDP values. Not extracted: Figure 2 chart of revenue including CIP (no printed values); the DSA primary-balance shock (an assumed 2% of GDP deterioration 'owing to a slowdown in CIP revenues', a stress assumption, not a CIP figure). Everything else is out of scope.
